Here’s a quick roundup of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thriller films released in 2020. These picks are based on critical consensus (Rotten Tomatoes / Metacritic), audience reception, and impact within the genre.

| # | Film | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern, tech‑savvy take on the classic horror story that doubles as a tense psychological thriller. Its tight pacing and strong female lead earned it a 96% score on Rotten Tomatoes. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Michelle Dockery | Ritchie’s signature fast‑cut style and witty dialogue make this heist‑drama feel fresh. It blends crime‑thriller with dark comedy, earning a 94% rating. |
| 3 | **The Night House** | David Bruckner | Rebecca Hall, Nathan Whitehead | A chilling psychological thriller that plays with perception and grief. Its atmospheric tension and Hall’s performance garnered a 93% score. |
| 4 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Lie Kaas | A Danish thriller that tackles social paranoia and moral ambiguity. Its stark realism and powerful performances earned a 92% rating. |
| 5 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | Though more historical drama, its courtroom thriller elements and moral complexity earned it a 91% rating. |
| 6 | **The Devil All the Time** | Antonio Campos | Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Riley Keough | A bleak, atmospheric crime‑drama that explores violence and faith across rural America. Its haunting tone and ensemble cast earned a 90% rating. |

### Quick Tips for Watching

- **Start with “The Invisible Man”** if you’re new to the genre; it’s the most accessible and has a great mix of horror and thriller elements.
- **Watch “The Hunt”** for a deeper dive into social commentary and moral complexity.
- **Pair “The Devil All the Time”** with a discussion on how environment shapes character choices.

Enjoy your crime‑thriller marathon!
